2027-03-12.title: Friday of the Fourth Week of Lent
readings: Let us condemn him to a shameful death
The Lord is close to the brokenhearted
They tried to arrest him, but his hour had not yet come
2027-03-12.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Friday of Lent: abstinence from meat (or another penance as your bishops' conference determines). Many parishes pray the Way of the Cross today.
2027-03-12.verse: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
theo: As Lent moves toward the Passion, the readings begin to sound like the plotting of Holy Week. The Book of Wisdom, written in Greek by a Jewish teacher in Alexandria not long before Christ, lets us overhear the thoughts of the ungodly. They have decided that life is short and ends in nothing, so they will enjoy it and crush anyone who gets in the way. And the one who gets in the way is the righteous man: “Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our actions.” His very life is a rebuke to them: “the very sight of him is a burden to us, because his manner of life is unlike that of others.” He calls God his Father. So they decide to test him: “if the righteous man is God's child, he will help him.” “Let us test him with insult and torture… Let us condemn him to a shameful death.” Christians have always heard in these words the voices at the foot of the cross: “He trusts in God; let God deliver him now” (Matthew 27:43). But the Wisdom writer adds the decisive line: “they did not know the secret purposes of God.” The Psalm gives the answer of faith: “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit… He keeps all their bones; not one of them will be broken”, words that John will see fulfilled on Calvary (John 19:36).

In the Gospel the danger is real. Jesus stays in Galilee because in Judea some were looking for a chance to kill him; when he goes up for the feast of Booths, he goes “not publicly but as it were in secret.” In John's Gospel “the Jews” here means the Jerusalem authorities who opposed Jesus; Jesus, his mother, his disciples and the crowds who welcomed him were themselves Jews, and the Church firmly rejects any blame of the Jewish people for his death (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 597). In the Temple, people argue: is this the Messiah? “Yet we know where this man is from.” Jesus cries out: “You know me, and you know where I am from. I have not come on my own. But the one who sent me is true… I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.” They know his village; they do not know his Father. “Then they tried to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.” Jesus is not a victim of chance. His hour is in the Father's hands, and when it comes he will give himself freely. On this Friday of abstinence, as we walk the Way of the Cross, we learn from him to trust our own hours to the Father: “My times are in your hand.”
outline: Ask: have you ever been disliked simply for doing what was right?
Wisdom 2 and the plot against the just.
Point 2 · His hour had not yet come
Jesus free and sovereign in his Passion.
“The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.”
live: Stand gently but firmly for what is right in one situation today, even if it costs you.
Walk the Way of the Cross
Pray the Stations today, at church or at home, and keep abstinence with love.
2027-03-12.prayer: Lord God, the righteous one was mocked and condemned, yet you were near to him and raised him up. Make us faithful when goodness is inconvenient, and teach us to place our times in your hands. Be near to all who are brokenhearted today. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Just One who was condemned to a shameful death offered himself freely when his hour came. At the altar that hour is made present: his Body given, his Blood poured out for us.

quick: The Book of Wisdom foretells the plot against the righteous man who calls God his Father.
Jesus speaks openly in the Temple; no one can seize him before his hour.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted.
2027-03-12.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today and keep the Friday abstinence.
2027-03-12.question: When goodness becomes inconvenient, do I hide or stand firm?

family.explain: Some people did not like Jesus because he was good and told the truth. They wanted to hurt him. But God was always close to him. When we are sad or hurt, God is close to us too.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or class who is sad or hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “When did someone stand up for what was right? Can we do that too?”

illus: A young engineer in a government office in Thiruvananthapuram refused to sign a false bill. For months he was mocked at tea breaks and left out of promotions. One Friday his old father found him praying the Stations alone in the parish church. The young man said: I am only walking with someone who was also inconvenient.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, righteous one, you were mocked for being good. Stay near to us when we are brokenhearted. Amen.
share: Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us (Wisdom 2:12). When has doing right made me unpopular?
No one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come (John 7:30). Do I trust my times to the Father?
The LORD is near to the brokenhearted (Psalm 34:18). Whose broken heart can I sit beside?
pm.resp: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith, that God may be near to them.
For whistle-blowers and all who suffer for honesty.
For the brokenhearted, the grieving and the depressed.
For friendship and respect between Christians and Jews.
For our group, that we may walk the Way of the Cross with love.
pm.close: Father, you are near to the brokenhearted. Keep us faithful in the hour of trial, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Book of Wisdom lets us hear the thoughts of people who have decided that life ends in nothing. Their plan is simple: enjoy everything and crush anyone who gets in the way. And who gets in the way? The righteous man. Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us (Wisdom 2:12).

His goodness is a silent rebuke. So they say: let us test him with insult and torture; let us condemn him to a shameful death. When we hear these words, we see the cross. But Wisdom adds: they did not know the secret purposes of God.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches openly in the Temple. They want to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come (John 7:30). Jesus is not trapped by events. When his hour comes, he will give his life freely, out of love for us.

Today is a Friday of Lent. We keep abstinence and many of us will walk the Way of the Cross. Let us walk with him, and let us not be afraid to be inconvenient for the sake of goodness. The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit (Psalm 34:18). Amen.
kids: Children, some people did not like Jesus because he was so good. But God was always close to him. When you are sad, remember: God is close to you too. Today, Friday, let us say thank you to Jesus for loving us all the way to the cross.

intro: Theme: “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted.”
The inconvenient righteous one, the hour in the Father's hands, and God's closeness in suffering.

q: Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us and opposes our actions; he reproaches us for sins against the law, and accuses us of sins against our training.
“If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.
points.apply: Do one right thing this week that you have been avoiding because it is unpopular.

points.h: His hour had not yet come
sub: They know his village, not his Father.
q: My times are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and persecutors.
Then they tried to arrest him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
points.apply: Each night this week, place tomorrow in the Father's hands with Psalm 31:15.

q: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
But rejoice insofar as you are sharing Christ's sufferings, so that you may also be glad and shout for joy when his glory is revealed.
points.apply: Pray the Way of the Cross this Friday and offer it for someone who is brokenhearted.

concl: The righteous one is hated for his goodness, but the plot of the wicked does not know God's purpose.
Jesus goes to his hour freely, and God is near to all who suffer with him.
2027-03-12.resolve: Pray the Way of the Cross every Friday until Good Friday.
